source_text: Ἡ τοίνυν ἔνστασις αὐτῶν καὶ ἡ πρόσφατος τοῦ ἀποσχίσματος αἵρεσις πρὸς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, τὴν αἰτίαν ἔσχε τοιαύτην· κώμη τις εἶναι λέγεται ἐν τῇ κατὰ τὴν Φρυγίαν Μυσίᾳ, καλουμένη Ἀρδαβαῦ τοὔνομα· ἔνθα φασὶ τινὰ τῶν νεοπίστων, πρώτως, Μοντανὸν τοὔνομα, κατὰ Γράτον Ἀσίας ἀνθύπατον, ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ ψυχῆς ἀμέτρῳ φιλοπρωτείας δόντα πάροδον εἰς ἑαυτὸν τῷ ἀντικειμένῳ, πνευματοφορηθῆναί τε καὶ αἰφνιδίως ἐν κατοχῇ τινὶ καὶ παρεκστάσει γενόμενον ἐνθουσιᾷν· ἄρξασθαί τε λαλεῖν καὶ ξενοφωνεῖν, παρὰ τὸ κατὰ παράδοσιν καὶ κατὰ διαδοχὴν ἄνωθεν τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἔθος δῆθεν προφητεύοντα· τῶν δὲ κατ’ ἐκεῖνο καιροῦ ἐν τῇ τῶν νόθων ἐκφωνημάτων ἀκροάσει γενομένων, οἱ μὲν ὡς ἐπὶ ἐνεργουμένῳ καὶ δαιμονῶντι καὶ ἐν πλάνης πνεύματι ὑπάρχοντι, καὶ τοὺς ὄχλους ταράττοντι ἀχθόμενοι ἐπετίμων, καὶ λαλεῖν ἐκώλυον· μεμνημένοι τῆς τοῦ Κυρίου διαστολῆς τε καὶ ἀπειλῆς, πρὸς τὸ φυλάττεσθαι τὴν τῶν ψευδοπροφητῶν ἐγρηγορότως παρουσίαν· οἱ δὲ ὡς ἁγίῳ πνεύματι καὶ προφητικῷ χαρίσματι ἐπαιρόμενοι· καὶ οὐχ ἥκιστα χαυνούμενοι· καὶ τῆς διαστολῆς τοῦ Κυρίου ἐπιλανθανόμενοι· τὸ βλαψίφρον καὶ ὑποκοριστικὸν καὶ λαοπλάνον πνεῦμα προὐκαλοῦντο· θελγόμενοι καὶ πλανώμενοι ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ, εἰς τὸ μηκέτι κωλύεσθαι (for. κωλύεσθαι λαλεῖν, καὶ) σιωπᾶν. τεχνῇ δέ τινι, μᾶλλον δὲ τοιαύτῃ μεθόδῳ κακοτεχνίας ὁ διάβολος τὴν κατὰ τῶν παρηκόων ἀπώλειαν μηχανησάμενος, καὶ παρ’ ἀξίαν ὑπ’ αὐτῶν τιμώμενος, ὑπεξήγειρέ τε καὶ προσεξέκαυσεν αὐτῶν τὴν ἀποκεκοιμημένην ἀπὸ τῆς κατ’ ἀλήθειαν πίστεως διάνοιαν· ὡς καὶ ἑτέρας τινὰς δύο γυναῖκας ἐπεγεῖραι, καὶ τοῦ νόθου πνεύματος πληρῶσαι· ὡς καὶ λαλεῖν ἐκφρόνως καὶ ἀκαίρως καὶ ἀλλοτριοτρόπως ὁμοίως τῷ προειρημένῳ. καὶ τοὺς μὲν χαίροντας καὶ καυχωμένους ἐπ’ αὐτῷ, μακαρίζοντος τοῦ πνεύματος, καὶ διὰ τοῦ μεγέθους τῶν ἐπαγγελμάτων ἐκφυσιοῦντος· ἔσθ’ ὅπῃ δὲ καὶ κατακρίνοντος στοχαστικῶς καὶ ἀξιοπίστως αὐτοὺς ἄντικρυς, ἵνα καὶ ἐλεγκτικὸν εἶναι δοκῇ· ὀλίγοι δ’ ἦσαν οὗτοι τῶν Φρυγῶν ἐξηπατημένοι· τὴν δὲ καθόλου καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανὸν ἐκκλησίαν βλασφημεῖν διδάσκοντος τοῦ ἀπηυθαδισμένου πνεύματος, ὅτι μήτε τιμὴν μήτε πάροδον εἰς αὐτὴν τὸ ψευδοπροφητικὸν ἐλάμβανε πνεῦμα. τῶν γὰρ κατὰ τὴν Ἀσίαν πιστῶν πολλάκις καὶ πολλαχῇ τῆς Ἀσίας εἰς τοῦτο συνελθόντων, καὶ τοὺς προσφάτους λόγους ἐξετασάντων καὶ βεβήλους ἀποφῃνάντων καὶ ἀποδοκιμασάντων τὴν αἵρεσιν, οὕτω δὴ τῆς τε ἐκκλησίας ἐξεώσθησαν, καὶ τῆς κοινωνίας εἴρχθησαν.
thought_title: Origin of the new prophecy in Ardabau
orientation: The author is beginning the written memorandum requested by the elders, explaining how the Montanist heresy first arose in a village of Phrygian Mysia.
pass_a_gloss: Their opposition, then, and the recent heresy of the schism against the church had this cause. A certain village is said to be in Mysia in the region of Phrygia, called Ardabau by name. There they say that one of the newly converted, first, Montanus by name, under Gratus the proconsul of Asia, in unbounded desire of the soul for love of preeminence gave entrance into himself to the adversary, and was carried by a spirit and suddenly becoming in a certain possession and ecstasy began to be possessed. And he began to speak and to make strange utterances, prophesying supposedly contrary to the custom of the church handed down by tradition and by succession from above. And of those who at that time came to hear the bastard utterances, some, as over one being worked upon and demonized and being in a spirit of error and troubling the crowds, being grieved, rebuked him and prevented him from speaking, remembering the Lord's distinction and threat, for the purpose of guarding against the coming of the false prophets watchfully. But others, as being elated by a holy spirit and prophetic gift, and not least being puffed up, and forgetting the Lord's distinction, called upon the mind-harming and flattering and people-deceiving spirit, being charmed and led astray by it, so that it might no longer be prevented from speaking and be silent. And by a certain art, or rather by such a method of evil art, the devil, having contrived the destruction of the disobedient, and being honored by them beyond what he deserved, stirred up and further inflamed their mind that had fallen asleep from the faith according to truth. So that he also raised up two other women and filled them with the bastard spirit, so that they also spoke out of their mind and untimely and in a foreign manner similarly to the one mentioned before. And those who were rejoicing and boasting over him, the spirit blessing them, and puffing them up through the greatness of the promises, and sometimes also condemning them conjecturally and plausibly outright, so that it might seem to be also capable of refutation. And few were these Phrygians who had been deceived. But the whole and entire church under heaven the self-willed spirit taught to blaspheme, because neither honor nor entrance into it did the false-prophetic spirit receive. For when the faithful throughout Asia had often and in many places of Asia come together for this purpose, and had examined the recent words and declared them profane and rejected the heresy, thus indeed they were expelled from the church and shut out from communion.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'ecstasy' for παρέκστασις, the key term for the Montanist frenzy.
The glossary requires 'to be possessed' for ἐνθουσιᾶν, describing the Montanist prophetic state.
νόθος means illegitimate or spurious; 'bastard' preserves the pejorative force against the false prophecy.
The passive infinitive indicates being borne or driven by a spirit, matching the author's claim of demonic agency.
διαστολή means a distinction or warning; the context is the Lord's warning to distinguish false prophets, so 'distinction' preserves the term's force.
ἀπαυθαδίζομαι means to be self-willed or presumptuous; this captures the spirit's arrogance in teaching blasphemy against the church.

bible_refs.note: τὴν τῶν ψευδοπροφητῶν ἐγρηγορότως παρουσίαν echoes the warning to beware of false prophets who come in sheep's clothing.

pass_b_english: Their opposition, then, and the recent heresy of their schism against the church had this origin. There is said to be a village in Mysia on the Phrygian border, called Ardabau. There, they say, one of the newly converted, named Montanus, in the time of Gratus, proconsul of Asia, gave entrance into himself to the adversary through an unbounded desire of soul for preeminence. He was carried by a spirit and, suddenly falling into some kind of possession and ecstasy, began to be possessed, and he started to speak and make strange utterances, supposedly prophesying contrary to the church's custom handed down by tradition and succession from the beginning.

Of those who were present at that time to hear the bastard utterances, some were distressed, treating him as one being worked upon, demonized, and in a spirit of error, and as one troubling the crowds. They rebuked him and tried to stop him from speaking, remembering the Lord's distinction and threat to keep watchful guard against the coming of false prophets (Matthew 7:15). Others, however, were elated as though by a holy spirit and a prophetic spiritual gift, and not least puffed up, forgetting the Lord's distinction. They invited the mind-harming, flattering, people-deceiving spirit, being beguiled and led astray by it, so that it could no longer be stopped from speaking or silenced.

By some artifice, or rather by such a method of evil cunning, the devil devised destruction for those who disobeyed. Since he was being honored by them beyond what he deserved, he stirred up and further inflamed their minds, which had fallen asleep from the faith that is according to truth. He even roused two other women and filled them with the bastard spirit, so that they too spoke frantically, untimely, and in a strange manner, just like the one mentioned before.

The spirit blessed those who rejoiced and boasted in it, puffing them up through the greatness of its promises, though at times it also condemned them outright with plausible, well-aimed accusations, so that it might seem to have the power to convict. But these were only a few of the Phrygians who had been deceived. The self-willed spirit taught them to blaspheme the whole church under heaven, because the false prophetic spirit received neither honor nor entrance into it.

For when the faithful throughout Asia had gathered many times and in many places of Asia for this purpose, and had examined the recent utterances and declared them profane, and had rejected the heresy, then indeed they were expelled from the church and barred from communion.

last_rejected.source_quote: εἰς τὸ μηκέτι κωλύεσθαι (for. κωλύεσθαι λαλεῖν, καὶ) σιωπᾶν
last_rejected.why: Source says 'so that they were no longer hindered from speaking and kept silent' — the silencing stopped, not the spirit.
last_rejected.fix: so that they were no longer prevented from speaking and silenced
last_rejected.ruling: Greek "εἰς τὸ μηκέτι κωλύεσθαι ... σιωπᾶν" means ‘no longer to be hindered (from speaking)’, i.e., cannot be silenced, matching the translation.

last_rejected.source_quote: Ἡ τοίνυν ἔνστασις αὐτῶν καὶ ἡ πρόσφατος τοῦ ἀποσχίσματος αἵρεσις πρὸς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν …
last_rejected.why: ἔνστασις means “ecstasy”, not “opposition”; the term is central to the argument and must be rendered as ecstasy.
last_rejected.fix: Their ecstasy, then, and the recent heresy of their schism against the church had this origin.
last_rejected.ruling: ἔνστασις here means 'opposition/insurrection,' not 'ecstasy' (ἐνθουσιᾷν/παρεκστάσις cover ecstasy later).

last_rejected.source_quote: ὡς καὶ ἑτέρας τινὰς δύο γυναῖκας ἐπεγεῖραι, καὶ τοῦ νόθου πνεύματος πληρῶσαι·
last_rejected.why: πνεῦμα is simply “spirit”; adding “bastard” introduces a false qualifier not in the source and violates the glossary.
last_rejected.fix: He even roused two other women and filled them with the spirit.
last_rejected.ruling: νόθου πνεύματος: 'bastard spirit' is correct; νόθου = 'bastard/illegitimate,' matching earlier νόθων.

last_rejected.quote: the devil devised destruction for those who disobeyed.
last_rejected.source_quote: τὴν κατὰ τῶν παρηκόων ἀπώλειαν μηχανησάμενος …
last_rejected.why: Greek says the devil planned the loss of the faithful (those who were faithful), not the loss of disobedient people; the agency is reversed.
last_rejected.fix: the devil devised the loss of the faithful.
last_rejected.ruling: παρηκόων = 'those who disobeyed/hearkened amiss'; not 'faithful.' Translation correctly renders it.
